newsitem.title: USA: Hemagen gets FDA clearance on CMV kit.
newsitem.headline: Hemagen gets FDA clearance on CMV kit.

text.p: Hemagen Diagnostics Inc. said Thursday it received Food and Drug Administration 510(k) clearance to market its Virgo ELISA CMV IgG kit.
The test detects current or past cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection. The Virgo ELISA CMV IgG test kit joins Hemagen's growing line of infectious disease test kits.

Carl Franzblau, president of Hemagen, said the Virgo CMV IgG test is produced in the increasingly popular ELISA (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) format and is the first in a series of Virgo ELISA kits to be produced in 1997. The test kit detects antibodies to cytomegalovirus (CMV) in human serum.

CMV infection may induce life-threatening conditions such as pneumonia, fever and hepatitis among immunosuppressed patients. CMV is a double-stranded DNA virus with characteristics common to members of the herpesvirus family.
The virus may remain in a latent state indefinitely following infection or it may emerge from time to time as an active infection.
